findings.title: Retry-count delete branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second `OR` branch (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) omits `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. This SMS cron therefore deletes every WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows. Today only this handler increments the column, but `retryCount` is a generic field on the shared model. Once any other scheduler (email/WhatsApp crons) starts using it, this job will silently delete those reminders. Put the `method: SMS` filter outside the `OR`, or add it to both branches.

findings.title: DB update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` block is not guarded. If it throws, the exception escapes the loop and the handler fails. Possible causes are a DB hiccup or the reminder being deleted concurrently, e.g. by booking cancellation, which makes the update raise P2025. All remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are then skipped, and the original error is never logged because the log line comes after the update. Log first and wrap the update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany`, which does not throw on missing rows.

findings.title: Reminders with no recipient or empty message still retry forever
findings.body: `retryCount` is only incremented when `scheduleSMS` returns falsy or throws. When `sendTo` is null/empty or `message` is empty, nothing is updated. Such reminders are re-fetched and reprocessed on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes, which is the behaviour this PR set out to stop. Increment retryCount (or delete the reminder) in that branch too.

findings.title: OR on unindexed retryCount defeats the existing index for the delete query
findings.body: The existing composite index is `(method, scheduled, scheduledDate)`, and `retryCount` has no index. An `OR` between an indexed predicate and an unindexed `retryCount > 1` predicate will typically force a sequential scan of the entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron invocation. Consider scoping the branch to `method = SMS, scheduled = false` so the index can be used, or running a separate targeted delete.
